conventions.convention: An experiment is a family of probability measures on one measurable observation space. It supplies neither a sigma-algebra on the parameter labels nor parameter measurability nor a common realization space.
The parametric model is the map from parameter labels to sampling laws; injectivity is not assumed.
A parameter-measurable kernel requires a supplied measurable parameter space, probability-measure sections, and measurable event-probability maps into [0,1] with its relative Borel sigma-algebra.
Observational equivalence means equality of measures on every measurable event, including when the parameter labels coincide.
An estimand is a function to a target set; neither parameter nor target measurability is imposed.
Identifiability has direction equal sampling laws imply equal target values. Model identifiability is identifiability of the identity target.
The unique factor map has domain exactly the image of the model map. Its construction is set-theoretic, uses no choice axiom, and asserts no measurable factorization.

load_bearing.statement: An experiment is a measurable space, a set of parameter labels, and a parameter-indexed family of probability measures on that space.

Its parametric statistical model is the parameter map P: Θ → the set of probability measures on the observation space, P(θ)=Pθ, regarded together with its parameter set and sample space. The map need not be injective.
An estimand ψ: Θ → T₀ is identifiable when Pθ=Pη implies ψ(θ)=ψ(η) for all θ,η∈Θ. The model is identifiable when its identity target is identifiable, equivalently when the model map is injective.
Two parameter values θ,η∈Θ are observationally equivalent if and only if Pθ=Pη, meaning agreement on every measurable event.
For a parametric model with parameter set Θ, an estimand or parameter target is a specified function ψ: Θ → T₀, where T₀ is a set of target values.

For a parametric model P: Θ → the set of probability measures on the observation space, an estimand ψ: Θ → T₀, and M=P(Θ), the following are equivalent: ψ is identifiable; ψ is constant on every observational equivalence class; there is a unique function ψ̄: M → T₀ such that ψ=ψ̄∘P. No measurable structure or measurable factor map is asserted.

seams_checked.note: The page and its experiment/estimand citations preserve arbitrary parameter labels. Statistics add a measurable target space separately; randomized procedures require data-to-action kernels without asserting parameter measurability or an auxiliary-seed representation. No reverse logical citation was found in the assigned pages or items.

Pointwise risk uses only the sampling law at each parameter. The joint-law lemma, Bayes-risk definition and posterior theorem explicitly add a measurable parameter space and model kernel; the posterior theorem further states its standard-Borel hypotheses. These uses do not infer kernel measurability from an arbitrary experiment. No reverse logical citation was found.

The dominated-experiment definition adds a supplied sigma-finite positive dominator while explicitly retaining the absence of parameter measurability. Likelihood densities are selected versions, and the page and definition assert neither measurable parameter dependence nor a parameter probability distribution. No reverse logical citation was found.

The IID estimator definition adds metric/Borel target structure without making the estimand parameter-measurable. The nonidentifiability theorem faithfully negates the identifiability implication, obtaining equal observation laws and distinct targets, then uses equal finite-product laws and disjoint target balls. The sample-mean theorem explicitly supplies its common IID realization space. No reverse logical citation was found.

The density-target definition treats selected Borel density versions as parameter labels and point evaluation as an estimand. It explicitly avoids claiming that point evaluation is identifiable from the law; the page preserves this version qualification. No reverse logical citation was found.
